title: Masking Personal Information
statement:
The string `s` is either an email address or a phone number. Return its masked form.

**Email.** It has the shape `name@domain`: `name` is two or more English letters (any case), and `domain` is English letters with one `'.'` that is neither its first nor its last character. To mask it, turn every letter into lowercase, and replace `name` by its first letter, then exactly five `'*'`, then its last letter (five stars even when `name` has only two letters). The `'@'` and the domain stay, lowercased.

**Phone number.** It holds 10 to 13 digits, possibly with characters from `'+'`, `'-'`, `'('`, `')'` and `' '` mixed in between. The final 10 digits are the local number and the 0 to 3 digits before them are the country code. To mask it, drop the separator characters and write `"***-***-DDDD"`, where `DDDD` are the last four digits. If the country code has `k > 0` digits, put `'+'`, then `k` stars, then `'-'` in front, e.g. `"+**-***-***-DDDD"` for `k = 2`.
constraints: s is a valid email address or a valid phone number
Email: 8 <= s.length <= 40, and s has only English letters plus exactly one '@' and exactly one '.'
Phone: 10 <= s.length <= 20, and s has only digits, spaces and the characters ( ) - +
notes:
## Intuition

The two kinds of input are easy to tell apart: only an email contains `'@'`. After that each case is plain string building. For an email we need the first letter, the last letter before `'@'` and everything from `'@'` on, all lowercased. For a phone number only the digits matter: how many there are decides the prefix, and the last four are the only ones shown.

## Approach

1. Find `at`, the position of `'@'`.
2. If it exists, lowercase `s` into `lower` and return `lower[0]`, five stars, `lower[at - 1]` and `lower.slice(at)`.
3. Otherwise collect every digit of `s` into `digits`.
4. Build `local` as `"***-***-"` plus the last four digits.
5. `countryLength = digits.length - 10`. If it is 0, return `local`.
6. Otherwise return `'+'`, `countryLength` stars, `'-'` and `local`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "LeetCode@LeetCode.com"` has `'@'` at `at = 8`. `lower` is `"leetcode@leetcode.com"`, so `lower[0] = 'l'`, `lower[7] = 'e'` and `lower.slice(8) = "@leetcode.com"`. Gluing them around the stars gives `"l*****e@leetcode.com"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one lowercase pass or one scan for digits over the `n` characters.
- Space: O(n): the lowercased copy or the digit string.

## Pitfalls

- The star count is always five, whatever the length of the name.
- Lowercase the domain too, not only the name.
- A `'+'` or other separator in the input says nothing about the country code; count digits instead.
- With no country code there is no leading `'+'` or `'-'`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `at` | index of `'@'`, or -1 for a phone number |
| `lower` | the email in lowercase |
| `digits` | the phone number's digits in order |
| `ch` | the character being examined |
| `local` | the masked local part, `"***-***-"` plus the last four digits |
| `countryLength` | how many digits form the country code (0 to 3) |

narration.2: Look for '@'; only an email address contains one.
narration.3: Found it, so s is an email.
narration.4: Lowercase the whole address, name and domain alike.
narration.5: Keep the first letter of the name, five stars, the last letter of the name (just before '@'), then '@' and the domain.
narration.7: Otherwise s is a phone number; gather its digits here.
narration.9: Only digits matter; separators are dropped.
narration.13: The local number always shows as three stars, three stars and its last four digits.
narration.14: Any digits beyond the ten local ones form the country code.
narration.16: Then the masked local number is the whole answer.
narration.18: Otherwise prefix '+', one star per country-code digit and a dash.
